subproblem.title: Vague limits versus closed-ball cylinder masses: μ(K_a) ≤ lim μ_j(K_b) and lim μ_j(K_a) ≤ μ(K_b) for a < b
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, G := Grassmannian N n and K_r := closedBall (0 : ℝ^N) r ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G. Let μs : ℕ → Measure(ℝ^N × G), and let μ be a measure on ℝ^N × G with VagueConverges μs μ: for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ), ∫ f dμs_j → ∫ f dμ in ℝ as j → ∞. (∫ is the Bochner integral, which is 0 for non-integrable integrands, as in Lean.) Let a < b be real and La, Lb ∈ [0, ∞]. Assume μ(K_b) ≠ ∞, μs_j(K_a) → La and μs_j(K_b) → Lb in [0, ∞] as j → ∞, and Lb ≠ ∞. Then μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (a b : ℝ) (La Lb : ℝ≥0∞), VagueConverges μs μ → a < b → μ (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≠ ∞ → Tendsto (fun j ↦ μs j (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) a ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))) atTop (𝓝 La) → Tendsto (fun j ↦ μs j (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))) atTop (𝓝 Lb) → Lb ≠ ∞ → μ (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) a ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≤ Lb ∧ La ≤ μ (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–5 of the parent proof for one fixed pair ρ < ρ' (here a < b), with the limiting masses abstracted to La and Lb.

Notation: G := Grassmannian N n and K_r := closedBall (0 : ℝ^N) r ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G. VagueConverges μs μ means ∫ f dμs_j → ∫ f dμ in ℝ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

1. (Cut-off.) Apply the sibling cylinder_cutoff (Lean: Submission.varifold_tangents_lbm_exists_cylinder_cutoff) to N, n, a, b and a < b. It gives F ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) such that every measure ν on ℝ^N × G with ν(K_b) ≠ ∞ satisfies ν(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dν) and ofReal(∫ F dν) ≤ ν(K_b).
2. (The limit measure.) Apply step 1 to ν = μ, which is allowed since μ(K_b) ≠ ∞: μ(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ μ(K_b).
3. (Eventual finiteness and comparison.) Since Lb < ∞, the set {c ∈ [0, ∞] : c < ∞} is an open neighbourhood of Lb (Iio ∞ ∈ 𝓝 Lb). So μs_j(K_b) → Lb implies μs_j(K_b) < ∞, i.e. μs_j(K_b) ≠ ∞, for all sufficiently large j. For each such j, step 1 with ν = μs_j gives μs_j(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) ≤ μs_j(K_b). Thus both inequalities hold eventually along atTop.
4. (Convergence of the cut-off integrals.) VagueConverges μs μ applied to f = F gives ∫ F dμs_j → ∫ F dμ in ℝ. Since ENNReal.ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is continuous, ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) → ofReal(∫ F dμ).
5. (Upper bound.) In the order-closed topology of [0, ∞], limits along the nontrivial filter atTop preserve eventual inequalities (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto). Apply this to the eventual inequality ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) ≤ μs_j(K_b) of step 3, with limits ofReal(∫ F dμ) (step 4) and Lb (hypothesis). This gives ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ Lb. With step 2, μ(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ Lb.
6. (Lower bound.) Apply the same principle to the eventual inequality μs_j(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) of step 3, with limits La (hypothesis) and ofReal(∫ F dμ) (step 4). This gives La ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ). With step 2, La ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ μ(K_b).
7. (Conclusion.) μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b).
proof_key_steps: Take the cut-off F of cylinder_cutoff for a < b. Since μ(K_b) < ∞, it gives μ(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫F dμ) ≤ μ(K_b).
Lb < ∞ forces μs_j(K_b) < ∞ eventually, so eventually μs_j(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫F dμs_j) ≤ μs_j(K_b).
VagueConverges and continuity of ENNReal.ofReal give ofReal(∫F dμs_j) → ofReal(∫F dμ).
Limits preserve eventual inequalities: ofReal(∫F dμ) ≤ Lb and La ≤ ofReal(∫F dμ); combining with the first step gives μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b).
